subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

She did her work **very good.**
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**good**" is an adjective, while "**well**" is an adverb.
 
• In this sentence, "**very good**" is incorrectly used to describe the verb "**did**," which requires an adverb.
 
• The correct usage is "**very well**" to describe how the work was done.
 
• The replacement ensures grammatical accuracy and clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She did her work very well."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "too well"** – This implies that the work was done excessively well, which changes the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 3: "quite good"** – This is incorrect because it uses the adjective "good" instead of the required adverb.
 
• **Option 4: "really great"** – Similar to Option 3, this uses an adjective instead of an adverb, making it grammatically incorrect.
